summary: Wachusett Mountain tower, Princeton MA: 1911 state fire watch in the Summit House, 1966 steel tower on the site; standing; sources disagree on the 1965 vs 1970 fire.

facts.design: 70-foot steel tower with 10 by 10 foot cab, built on the site in 1966
facts.status_note: NHLR says the 1966 tower continues in active service. A March 2012 visit report says the current tower was to be dismantled. No source read says which structure stands today.

staffing.status: staffed seven days a week in fire season or at Class 3 (High) fire danger, per undated Gardner News report; seasonal staffing per March 2012 NHLR visit

access.note: The cab is not accessible to the general public, per the March 4, 2012 NHLR visit report. A visitor observation deck was not yet open then, and no source confirms it opened. The public climbing of the old wooden stairway was discontinued by 1961 for fire hazard.

facts.agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control

events.note: State fire watch established in 1911 and staffed an observation room atop the Summit House; FFLOS calls it the first Massachusetts state fire lookout
Warden J. Harry Allen detected a barn fire three miles west of Princeton center; barn struck by lightning and destroyed, $300 loss
Newspaper item: 485 fires reported from the Wachusett tower in the year before, the most of 24 state observation stations
Observer James Maley, of many years, to be replaced by Mr. Skinner of Princeton
Daily operation halted three years earlier; tower still maintained on high-fire days; public climbing of wooden stairway discontinued for fire hazard
Summit House containing the fire lookout burned, per NHLR and the Forest Lookouts page. FFLOS dates the lookout room to 1911-1965.
70-foot steel tower with 10x10 cab built on the site, replacing the destroyed lookout
Summit House burned December 18, 1970, per Princeton Historical Society; FFLOS says around 1970
Registered December 15, 2003 as US 539, MA 6; nominated by Henry Isenberg
Registered September 3, 2008 as US 51, MA 51, nominated by Henry Isenberg
Visit report March 4, 2012 (Robert Young): new visitor observation deck brand new and not yet open; cab not accessible to general public; current tower to be dismantled

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR names the Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control as administrator. The Gardner News report says the Department of Conservation and Recreation operates the towers. The story names the register's agency and does not choose between the two.
NHLR and FFLOS place the tower on Wachusett Mountain in Worcester County, and the register calls it the Princeton Fire Tower. The Gardner News report says Westminster. The story names both.
NHLR gives 1,977 ft (603 m) and FFLOS gives 2,006 ft (611 m) for the same coordinates. The brief's 602.6 m matches NHLR. Elevation is not a facts key, so it is left out of facts.

sources.title: What's that tower on top of Mount Wachusett? Why fire departments are glad it's there

notes_for_editor: Five sources read. The early history (1911 fire watch, 1912 and 1915 items, 1923 observer change, 1961 status) comes from the Forest Lookouts newspaper excerpts. These are transcriptions on a hobbyist site and were not checked against the original newspapers. Unresolved: (1) the Summit House burn date, 1965 (NHLR, Forest Lookouts) against around 1970 (FFLOS) and 12/18/1970 (Princeton Historical Society); the story reports both. (2) Whether the 1966 tower is the one standing today. The 2012 NHLR visit says the current tower was to be dismantled. A search snippet of a 2012 FFLA Massachusetts Facebook photo caption says a current tower was near the end of construction, but that post was not readable, so it is not cited. (3) The Gardner News copy has no date, so 'today' staffing is undated. Its town (Westminster) differs from the register. Not verified: current public access and whether the observation deck opened. No photos added.
